system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

tools.description: List the files in the audit workspace.
tools.name: list_files

tools.description: Read one workspace file. Lines are numbered.
tools.name: read_file

path.description: File name inside the workspace, e.g. inventory.py

parts.text:
Audit step 1: Enumerate the inventory-service workspace recursively and list every file it contains (source, tests, config, build and dependency manifests), so the audit scope is complete.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.

{"step": 1, "files": ["report.py", "README.md", "inventory.py"], "defects": [{"file": "inventory.py", "line": 8, "explanation": "average_daily_sales divides by len(sales), which raises ZeroDivisionError when sales is an empty list."}, {"file": "inventory.py", "line": 21, "explanation": "range(1, len(items)) starts at index 1, so the first item is never checked and low_stock misses it."}, {"file": "report.py", "line": 5, "explanation": "The file opened here is never closed (no with block or close call), so the handle leaks and written data may not be flushed."}]}

Audit step 2: Audit the source files for logic defects such as off-by-one errors, wrong stock or quantity arithmetic, unchecked null or missing values, and incorrect comparisons, recording the file and line number for each.
Use the list_files and read_file tools on the workspace. Report the files and the defects you found with file and line.
